newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Russian official to visit Kuwait after Iraq oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Russian official to visit Kuwait after Iraq oil deal.

text.p: A senior Russian diplomat on Tuesday will visit Kuwait, which has expressed concern over a new Moscow-Baghdad oil deal, diplomats said on Monday.

The head of the Middle East department at Russia's foreign ministry, Andrey Vdovin, is due to arrive in Kuwait late on Tuesday night at the start of a Gulf tour for official talks on Wednesday with senior Kuwaiti officials, they said.
"Kuwait has expressed its deep concern" over Friday's Russia-Iraqi deal, one diplomat said, "and I'm sure they (Kuwaiti officials) will raise the issue with Vdovin."
The 23-year deal is for the development of seven to eight billion barrels of reserves in southern Iraq's west Qurnah oilfield.
Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov said the $3.5 billion project would be implemented regardless of the United Nations sanctions imposed on Iraq since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

But Zarubezhneft deputy chairman Yuri Agababov, whose firm has a stake in the deal, said on Monday: "The U.N. sanctions will be fully observed. We are not looking to violate any sanctions. The only things that will go forward now are things that do not violate the sanctions."
